JEREL: Jerel received Louisiana state's Principal of the Year in our fourth year together and is now CEO of Collegiate Academies.
CV: I first started working with Jerel Bryant as a consultant. Jerel was the founding principal of Collegiate Academies Carver High School, then in its third year. He was (and still is) a really compelling and charismatic leader. At the time, his school was really struggling with academic results, student culture and community relations. I was tasked with answering the question: do we keep this leader, can he be successful? Jerel had created a relatively strong adult culture that had started to fray as student behavior and instruction deteriorated. While his staff loved him, the school lacked a clear vision and had almost no systems. Jerel struggled with follow through and reliability. The school grew, as many do, out of a very strong founding school (Sci Academy) where teacher quality was high and systems were less necessary as each individual was so strong (and had their own systems and structures) When I arrived I found teachers highly frustrated with students and operating as "negative controllers" and students responding by pushing back, skipping class, opting out of learning. Knowing we had a high potential leader in Jerel, I sought to build him up as the model for how we should be operating with students and helped him build enabling systems to help the school function smoothly. I did this by primarily working shoulder to shoulder with him and giving him incredibly high doses of real time feedback - primarily affirming feedback that empowered him and built his confidence to help him stop second guessing himself. He had handcuffed himself with negative self talk. He was receiving a lot of feedback telling him that things were not good enough, but not a lot of recognition for his incredible strengths or technical support to address this gaps in his leadership. There was an operations director that spiked high in follow through and attention to detail and instead of complimenting Jerel's leadership and working as a solid team, their relationship had frayed and it seemed like nearly everything the other did was used as evidence to support the hypothesis that the school was failing because of the other person. I clearly named that this frayed relationship needed to be reset and helped them come into alignment, focusing them on results and impact rather than narratives of blame. I helped create simple, clear systems for school operation and behavior to stabilize the culture I helped the staff see how their attempts at holding high expectations were ineffective because of their inconsistency , their lack of credibility and their palpable frustration with the students. We turned the corner helping teachers become "no nonsense nurturers / warm demanders" building strong relationships by being more consistent, removing some punitive consequences that seemed petty to students and families, by re-injecting joy into the school day. I helped Jerel be the leader of the campus by getting out of his office and on to the floor - we spent hours and hours real time coaching and modelling. Jerel was very good as a teacher and was good with student interactions, so we took the approach that we needed to put that on stage and show teachers and students what it looks like to effectively invest, direct and redirect scholars. It worked. Students started to feel like school was safe, predictable and purposeful. After a year as consultant, I joined on (in part because of the success we had with Jerel) as Chief Culture Officer. Over the next five years, I helped Jerel grow his school to double its size, decrease suspension by 75% (truly) and increase student satisfaction by 50%. I learned the power of strength based coaching and of explicit relationship repair. I also learned how essential it is that I build strong relationships so that I can deliver direct feedback without having to apologize or couch it with fluff. It was this directness on top of the trust I built with Jerel that ultimately helped him see the problem. I was then able to help him develop the technical skills of systems creation and management and build a highly aligned and high functioning leadership team that helped guide the school to rapid growth across the board Jerel received Louisiana state's Principal of the Year in our fourth year together and is now CEO of Collegiate Academies AND the principal of an ~800 student high school. When asked to write a recommendation for my work, he wrote: "The work with Chris Habetler deeply accelerated the trajectory of my school and ultimately the network at large. To this day, when we make decisions, I think about the work Chris and I did together. Chris's work was nothing short of transformational"
